action: Resample AAPL Alpaca 1-min bars to daily OHLCV and compute 10 core Bucket-48 daily features
alternatives_considered: Download fresh daily OHLCV from Alpaca REST API instead of resampling from 1-min (more canonical data, but adds API round-trips and rate-limit risk)
Use yfinance daily data as source (avoids resampling edge-case bugs, but introduces data-source consistency questions vs the existing Alpaca pipeline)
Run multi-ticker batch (MSFT+NVDA+AAPL) first pass (more representative but triples debug surface and risk of silent errors in early code)
Skip daily entirely; test Bucket-48 features at existing 5-min resolution with XGBoost (higher effort, no regime change from the 7 failed variants)
why_chosen: Daily resolution is the single most likely source of edge per previous analysis (7/7 intraday variants failed), and resampling existing 1-min Alpaca bars avoids new API dependencies, rate limits, or data-source inconsistency — AAPL first because it has the most complete 1-min history and the cleanest resample boundary.
expected_outcome: Daily AAPL DataFrame with 1,260 rows and 10 feature columns written to parquet, confirmed by row-count and column-list assertion.
risk_factors: 1-min bar gaps at session boundaries (Alpaca drops first/last minute intermittently) could produce bad daily open/high/low/close if the first or last bar of the day is missing during resample
closed='left' resample semantics with reindex might infer a daily bar for days with zero trading (weekends, holidays), producing a flat line bar that pollutes features
rollback_strategy: Delete the daily parquet output — the 1-min source parquet is read-only and untouched; full rollback cost < 1 second.

action: Walk-forward backtest daily RSI<30 mean reversion on AAPL: 2yr IS / 1yr OOS / 1yr step, hold 21 days
alternatives_considered: Daily RSI<30 AND daily close < 20-day SMA as entry (two-condition gate that filters out RSI dips in already-broken downtrends — more conservative but reduces n_trades by ~40%)
Daily RSI<30 with VWAP-anchored exit instead of fixed-duration hold (dynamic exit that might improve PF but adds a session-boundary complexity to daily signals)
No-lookahead stochastic RSI<20 instead of standard RSI<30 (more extreme filter, fewer trades, higher expected WR if reversion is real)
why_chosen: RSI<30 on daily bars is the single most replicated mean-reversion finding in academic finance (Jegadeesh 1990, Lehmann 1990, Gutierrez-Kelley 2009) — if this doesn't produce PF≥1.10 on AAPL across 4 OOS folds, the daily-frequency hypothesis fails the most basic sanity check and we should abandon periodicity as the variable in favor of cross-sectional strategies.
expected_outcome: WF report with 4 fold results showing either (a) WR≥52% and PF≥1.10 in at least 3 of 4 folds, or (b) uniformly negative results that conclusively reject the daily mean-reversion hypothesis for AAPL.
risk_factors: 21-day fixed hold period is arbitrary and may exit winners too early or losers too late — a regime-dependent optimal holding period could exist but we won't find it on the first pass
The 2-year IS / 1-year OOS split may not capture enough RSI<30 events in the OOS window (bull market with few deep dips) to reach statistical significance — OOS could have n<10 trades
rollback_strategy: Delete the WF output CSV and equity curve CSV for AAPL daily — the daily parquet from s1 is read-only and shared; no side effects beyond the strategy output directory.

action: Run cross-sectional decile-long/short backtest on 100 S&P 500 tickers using 21-day momentum
alternatives_considered: Run single-ticker daily momentum at the ticker level (AAPL) instead of cross-sectional — similar to what s2 does for RSI, but momentum is inherently a cross-sectional phenomenon and single-ticker momentum tests are known to be weak in liquid equities
Wait until all 500 tickers have daily parquet before running cross-sectional backtest (cleaner, but blocks progress on strategy testing for 30+ min while data pipeline finishes)

Use existing 1-min data directly without daily resample, aggregating to daily via pandas resample within the backtest loop (avoids creating intermediate parquet files but makes the backtest slower due to repeated 1-min→daily conversion on each iteration)
why_chosen: The cross-sectional momentum anomaly (Jegadeesh-Titman 1993) is the most replicated anomaly in empirical finance and directly orthogonal to the failed mean-reversion approaches — 100 tickers is a sufficient sample to detect a long-short spread if it exists, and running it now on tickers we can resample from existing 1-min parquet avoids the multi-hour wait for all 500. Note: s3 actually needs daily data for 100 tickers, not just AAPL — the depend_on should be interpreted as requiring the daily resample module from s1 plus parallel execution of that module across 100 tickers. If only AAPL daily data exists, the step must first batch-resample 100 tickers or pull daily data directly from the 1-min parquet at runtime.
expected_outcome: Single CSV file with decile 1-10 average daily returns, long-short cumulative return, and Sharpe ratio across 4 OOS folds — either confirming the momentum anomaly survives in this S&P 500 subset (Sharpe > 0.5) or rejecting it for this universe and timeframe.
risk_factors: 100 tickers' daily data must exist or be generated first — if s1 only created AAPL daily, s3 will fail on first ticker after AAPL. The module must either batch-resample or fall back to inline pandas resample from 1-min with a progress-bar per ticker

21-day momentum in a 2022-2025 period that includes a sharp bear (2022) then strong bull (2023-24) may show regime-dependence where momentum works in one half and reverses in the other — the 4 OOS fold structure should detect this but the aggregate average may hide regime-contingent behavior
rollback_strategy: Delete the cross_sectional_results.csv output file. The 1-min parquet source files are read-only; the daily resample intermediate files are regeneratable. Full rollback in < 5 seconds.

action: Kill this Claude process immediately — load 29 (cap=12), sustained cap breach for 30+ min, same VM compressor trajectory that caused kernel panic
alternatives_considered: Continue running and hope load drops naturally (no evidence this happens — load climbed from 10→14→30 over 30h)
Spawn an OpenClaw sub-agent to offload work first (would add more memory pressure before any offload benefit)
Suspend non-critical daemons via launchctl to reduce system load (daemons already at 12/37 UP — cannot reduce further without breaking core infra)
why_chosen: Load at 29+ is triple the 12 cap with same VM compressor signature that caused the 16:37:11 kernel panic — every minute of delay increases probability of forced reboot which loses all daemons vs clean kill which preserves everything on disk.
expected_outcome: Load drops below 8 within 2 minutes. All 10 artifacts, ~92% recovery state, and 4 guardrail audits survive on disk for next session.
risk_factors: Kernel panic during kill window — kill -9 on high-load system under VM pressure could wedge the process instead of cleanly exiting
Launchd may lose track of 3 SIGTERM daemon plists during process kill if they're mid-respawn
rollback_strategy: Process termination is irreversible — next Claude Code or OpenClaw session reads current filesystem state. All work is in files (10 artifacts, ~/.zg/hooks/, settings.json), not in volatile memory. No rollback needed.
